text.arabic_uthmani: جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ يَدْخُلُونَهَا يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍۢ وَلُؤْلُؤًۭا ۖ وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌۭ

words.gloss_range: plural gardens as the named reward-domain, tracked later as one feminine-singular container
words.root_gloss_range: covering, enclosure, hiddenness, protection, garden growth, and unseen-being branches; the local noun selects the garden/enclosure branch
words.prose: {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ}} ({{tr:jannātu}}) opens by naming the reward as a place before any action is narrated. Its plural form gives abundance, while the later object and locative pronouns treat that abundance as one garden-domain entered, adorned within, and inhabited. The {{ar:ج ن ن}} ({{tr:j-n-n}}) cover-field makes the gardens an enclosed, protected interior, but the local feminine plural noun, entry verb, and repeated locatives keep the sense on gardens rather than unseen beings. The phrase also concretizes the great bounty of 35:32 into a sensory reward scene and joins a recognizable paradise-entry and adornment formula, including the contrast with 13:23 where the same destination-entry shape expands through kinship.

topics.headline: fronted reward domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first receives the reward as a named residence, so entry and adornment unfold inside a place already placed before the listener.
topics.reason: The nominative opening phrase is followed by the entry predicate, so the scene begins with destination before motion.

topics.headline: plural gardens as one container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that many gardens are grammatically compressed into one domain by the recurring feminine-singular pronoun.
topics.reason: The object suffix in word 3 and both locative suffixes in words 5 and 14 refer back to the garden phrase.

topics.headline: enclosed garden root-field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the gardens as protective interior space, while avoiding a shift into the unseen-being branch of the root.
topics.reason: The root has concealment and unseen branches, but the local noun, entry object, and repeated garden locatives select the garden/enclosure branch.

topics.headline: formula and boundary shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 35:32's abstract bounty become a known paradise display, with 13:23 showing a related formula pointed toward family entry rather than adornment.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete boundary and inter-ayah references, and the local ayah immediately fills the formula with entry, gold, pearl, and silk.

words.gloss_range: fixed genitive abode-name that classifies the gardens as abiding residence
words.root_gloss_range: settling, staying, remaining fixed, embedded deposit, and other distant branches; the local construct selects abiding residence
words.prose: {{ar:عَدْنٍ}} ({{tr:ʿadnin}}) is not a loose adjective after the gardens; as the genitive second term of the construct, it makes permanence part of the destination's name. Entry therefore moves into an abode already marked by abiding, not into a temporary scene later made stable. The broader {{ar:ع د ن}} ({{tr:ʿ-d-n}}) evidence supports staying and fixed deposit, so the mine-place branch can sharpen embedded permanence, while the local grammar keeps the selected force on settled residence. Cross-passage rows show the same formula in 9:72, 13:23, 16:31, and 61:12, but 35:33 unfolds it through visible honor rather than leaving it as a title.

topics.headline: construct abode-name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees permanence built into the garden category before the entry verb begins.
topics.reason: The word is genitive as the second term of the construct headed by word 1, so it classifies the gardens.

topics.headline: settled root pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the residence as fixed and abiding, with the deposit image reinforcing permanence without replacing the local abode-name.
topics.reason: V4 evidence supports staying and fixed-deposit branches, but the local construct phrase selects the reward-abode use.

topics.headline: formulaic abode echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the abode formula as stable across passages while noticing that this ayah fills it with entry, jewelry, and silk.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete formula references, and local continuation specifies the formula through embodied reward.

words.gloss_range: active imperfect plural entry with attached garden object pronoun
words.root_gloss_range: entering, access, threshold-crossing, admission, interiority, and negative intrusion/defect branches; the local frame selects honorable access into the gardens
words.prose: {{ar:يَدْخُلُونَهَا}} ({{tr:yadkhulūnahā}}) carries the chosen group from 35:32 as an implicit masculine-plural subject and makes the gardens a direct object through the hā suffix. That direct object turns reward into threshold-crossing, not merely a state of blessing, and the same pronoun later becomes the locative domain for adornment and clothing. The imperfect active form stages the entry as unfolding motion, while the passive yudkhalūnahā reading would construe admission as something done to them. The {{ar:د خ ل}} ({{tr:d-kh-l}}) root's inside/access field survives, but intrusion and defect branches are blocked by the paradise destination. The 13:23 parallel keeps the entry formula audible, though 35:33 moves from entry directly into bodily adornment.

topics.headline: implicit entrants and object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the selected inheritors into the scene without needing them renamed, and sees the gardens as the crossed object.
topics.reason: The verb has 3mp agreement and an attached feminine-singular object pronoun referring to the gardens.

topics.headline: threshold access root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader imagines reward as crossing from outside into protected interior space, while negative intrusion senses remain excluded.
topics.reason: The direct garden object selects honorable access, not hidden defect or hostile intrusion.

topics.headline: active and passive entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that canonical active entry foregrounds their crossing, while the variant would foreground admitted access.
topics.reason: The canonical form is active imperfect, while the CRITICAL variant evidence gives a passive admission construal.

topics.headline: formula pivot to adornment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the familiar paradise-entry formula become the hinge into the ayah's later jewelry and clothing display.
topics.reason: The same object pronoun recurs as both later locatives, and rows cite 13:23 as a related entry formula.

words.gloss_range: passive Form II adornment applied to the same plural entrants
words.root_gloss_range: ornamenting, jewelry, pleasing sweetness, beautified state, and self-adornment branches; the local passive selects externally bestowed adornment
words.prose: {{ar:يُحَلَّوْنَ}} ({{tr:yuḥallawna}}) changes the group's role: after active entry, they become recipients of bestowed adornment. The passive suppresses the adorner and lets the transformed state stand forward, while the Form II pattern keeps the action as applied beautification rather than mere inner pleasantness. The following locative and min asāwira phrase make the root's adornment field concrete: honor appears on bodies as bracelets, gold, and pearl. The 18:31 and 22:23 formula is reused after inheritance language, and the 35:12 echo shifts from human wearing of extracted ornament to eschatological adornment received inside the reward scene.

topics.headline: passive bestowed adornment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same group move from active entrants to recipients whose status is conferred on them.
topics.reason: The verb is passive with a 3mp subject agreement and no expressed agent.

topics.headline: concrete jewelry cluster
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees honor become tangible and body-worn, not just an abstract declaration of favor.
topics.reason: The passive verb governs the garden locative and bracelet phrase, and the row cluster ties the verb to bracelets, gold, and pearl.

topics.headline: variant and echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes canonical external adornment from a possible pleasing-state reading, and sees 35:12, 18:31, and 22:23 as concrete comparanda.
topics.reason: The canonical local form is passive adornment; variant and inter-ayah rows sharpen contrast without replacing the local parse.

words.gloss_range: first fused locative, in it/within it, referring to the gardens
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) places the adornment inside the garden-domain already entered. The pronoun returns to the gardens, so the jewelry is not a threshold gift or a detached possession; it belongs to life within that residence. Its position before the min asāwira phrase fixes where the transformation occurs before the verse specifies what adornment consists of. Because the same locative returns in the clothing clause, this first {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) starts the repeated containment frame that binds ornaments and garments to one place.

topics.headline: garden locative for adornment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the adornment as an interior condition of the gardens, not as a loose reward item.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is attached to the passive adornment verb, and the suffix refers to the gardens.

topics.headline: repeated containment frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same place governs both body layers: applied ornaments and later silk clothing.
topics.reason: The later locative repeats the same fused preposition-pronoun form and garden antecedent.

words.gloss_range: first preposition narrowing adornment to bracelet class or medium
words.prose: The first {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) begins the controlled descent from adornment as a state to bracelets as its medium or selected class. It keeps the phrase prepositional rather than making bracelets a bare direct object, and it leaves both specification and partitive pressure available. Because another min follows before gold, the first particle initiates a two-step architecture: adornment is narrowed to bracelet form, then bracelet form is narrowed to material.

topics.headline: first class-medium min
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees bracelets as the mediated form of adornment, not as a loose object after the passive verb.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the bracelet noun in the adornment phrase.

topics.headline: two-step min narrowing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause move by nested specification from adornment to bracelet to gold substance.
topics.reason: The next preposition repeats the same form before the material noun, producing a class-to-material chain.

words.gloss_range: plural bracelets as the first concrete ornament class, governed by the first min and qualified by the second
words.root_gloss_range: bracelet, enclosing wall, raised boundary, section, scaling, rank, and other branches; the local phrase selects bracelets while preserving encircling imagery
words.prose: {{ar:أَسَاوِرَ}} ({{tr:asāwira}}) is the hinge of the adornment phrase: it is governed by the first min, qualified by the second, and close enough to pearl for coordination. As the first concrete item after the passive adornment verb, it turns bestowed status into visible objects on the body. The {{ar:س و ر}} ({{tr:s-w-r}}) field includes walls and boundaries, so the bracelet branch miniaturizes enclosure onto the wrist; the local adornment verb and gold material keep the sense on bracelets, not walls or scaling. The plural broken form multiplies status markers, and 18:31, 22:23, 43:53, and 76:21 show the bracelet-material field as a recurring paradise adornment pattern with varying material registers.

topics.headline: bracelet syntax hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees bracelets carry the transition from adornment class to gold material and pearl coordination.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the first preposition, qualified by the second material phrase, and participates in the adornment list.

topics.headline: encircling root image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels enclosure scaled down from garden space to body-worn rings, while local grammar blocks wall or climbing senses.
topics.reason: V4 supports wall and bracelet branches, but the passive adornment frame and gold material select bracelets.

topics.headline: plural paradise bracelets
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices multiple status markers and a recurrent reward motif whose material can vary across passages.
topics.reason: Rows cite plural form pressure and concrete references for bracelet materials across 18:31, 22:23, 43:53, and 76:21.

topics.headline: sonic expansion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ornament word widen audibly between the clipped prepositions before the phrase narrows to material.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows describe the local sound pattern between the two prepositions.

words.gloss_range: second preposition marking gold as material/explanatory complement of bracelets
words.prose: The second {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) governs gold, so gold is the material of the bracelets rather than a separate coordinate prize. Because the governed noun is a mass material, this preposition leans more strongly toward composition and explanation than the first min, which opens a bracelet class. The repeated particle keeps the syntax moving by nested specification rather than by a flat list.

topics.headline: gold material min
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands gold as the bracelets' material, not as an independent reward item competing with pearl.
topics.reason: The second preposition governs the genitive material noun and attaches to the bracelet phrase.

topics.headline: nested specification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees material value subordinated to wearable form through repeated prepositional narrowing.
topics.reason: The two prepositions repeat the same form while changing governed nouns from ornament class to substance.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive mass noun specifying gold as bracelet material
words.root_gloss_range: gold as concrete metal and going-away/departure as verbal branch; local grammar selects material gold while allowing contrastive echo
words.prose: {{ar:ذَهَبٍ}} ({{tr:dhahabin}}) is genitive under the second min, so it names the substance of the bracelets rather than a separate coordinate object. Its indefinite mass form gives material quality, not counted units. The broader {{ar:ذ ه ب}} ({{tr:dh-h-b}}) root includes going-away, but local morphology locks the word into the concrete gold noun; that departure branch survives as contrast because 35:34 immediately uses the same root for grief going away. The same metal also shifts value across passages: 9:34 presents hoarded gold under judgment, while 35:33 turns gold into bestowed adornment, and 18:31, 22:23, and 43:53 keep the gold-bracelet pairing formulaic.

topics.headline: genitive gold material
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads gold as bracelet substance and material quality, not as an itemized second prize.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the material preposition and depends on the bracelet phrase.

topics.headline: departure root contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a root associated with going away become stable precious material here, then return as removal in 35:34.
topics.reason: The local word is a concrete noun, so the motion branch cannot govern the parse; it remains a contrastive echo.

topics.headline: gold value echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees gold's value re-situated from hoarding and status display into bestowed paradise adornment.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite 9:34 and the bracelet-gold recurrence in 18:31, 22:23, and 43:53.

words.gloss_range: additive conjunction before pearl, reopening the adornment field after gold material specification
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) reopens the adornment catalogue after the nested gold-bracelet phrase. It adds pearl while leaving the attachment question live: in the standard accusative reading pearl can stand as an added adornment item, while the genitive variant can fold it nearer to the material phrase with gold. The prefixed conjunction makes the expansion immediate in recitation, shifting the phrase from material specification to added radiance.

topics.headline: pearl expansion wa
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the catalogue reopen after gold, so the luxury field is not exhausted by the bracelet material.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates pearl with the preceding adornment phrase.

topics.headline: attachment ambiguity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector keeps pearl available either as added adornment or, under variant case, as material alongside gold.
topics.reason: The local conjunction links pearl but does not by itself settle whether pearl is coordinated with bracelets or with material in variant readings.

words.gloss_range: accusative pearl as added adornment, with accepted genitive and hamza-easing variants affecting attachment and sound
words.root_gloss_range: pearl and glittering radiance as quadriliteral object-root; no local verbal action branch is selected
words.prose: {{ar:لُؤْلُؤًۭا}} ({{tr:luʾluʾan}}) completes the jewelry beat before the ayah turns to clothing. In the standard accusative it stands as an added adornment item; the genitive luʾluʾin reading would fold pearl nearer to the preceding material phrase. Its quadriliteral repetition and paired hamzas make the word bead-like and bright in sound, while easing readings such as lūluʾ soften that texture without changing the referent. The local noun selects actual pearl, not a derived action, and the 56:23 image of protected pearl becomes public display here; 22:23 supplies the closest full paradise-luxury cluster.

topics.headline: pearl case hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees pearl as the local hinge where case decides whether it is an added item or another material under the previous phrase.
topics.reason: The standard word is accusative and coordinated, while CRITICAL rows preserve the genitive variant as a material-attachment possibility.

topics.headline: radiant pearl object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader receives pearl as concentrated, protected brightness brought into display, while false verbal derivation is excluded.
topics.reason: The noun-root evidence supports pearl and glitter pressure, but no productive action sense governs the local parse.

topics.headline: sound and variant texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the bead-like repetition and glottal sparkle of the word, with qiraat easing changing texture rather than meaning.
topics.reason: The phonetic and qiraat rows distinguish articulation from grammatical attachment.

topics.headline: pearl paradise echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees hidden pearl imagery from 56:23 become visible adornment here, within the full luxury cluster also found at 22:23.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete references for protected pearl and the full paradise adornment cluster.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a new nominal clothing clause
words.prose: This {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is not another item in the jewelry list. It resumes with a fresh nominal clause, shifting from ornaments applied to the body to clothing possessed by the entrants. The conjunction still keeps the clothing connected to the same reward display, but it marks a new syntactic layer: the body-display broadens from wrist ornaments and adornment materials to a full garment state.

topics.headline: garment clause pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader catches the syntactic and visual turn from jewelry inventory to a full clothing predicate.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the coordinated nominal clause beginning with the clothing subject.

topics.headline: continuity with separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clothing clause as connected to the adornment scene but not swallowed by it.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates clauses while the following nominative subject starts a separate predication.

words.gloss_range: nominative possessed clothing subject, singular collective in sense, introducing the final nominal predication
words.root_gloss_range: wearing, covering, garment, armor, protective covering, confusion/obscuring, and close involvement branches; the local phrase selects honorable clothing/covering
words.prose: {{ar:لِبَاسُهُمْ}} ({{tr:libāsuhum}}) begins the final nominal clause as a nominative subject: their clothing there is silk. The hum suffix ties garments to the same entrants and contrasts with passive adornment: one layer is done to them, the other is theirs. The singular collective form names attire as a state rather than enumerating garments, and the zero-copula clause stabilizes the scene after motion and adornment. The {{ar:ل ب س}} ({{tr:l-b-s}}) field selects garment covering here; armor and confusion branches remain only contrastive pressure because the possessive garment noun and silk predicate make honorable covering clear. The 7:26 moral clothing echo becomes material silk here, while 35:12 shifts from active wearing of extracted goods to possessed clothing in paradise.

topics.headline: nominal possessed clothing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final body layer stated as their possessed condition, not as another passive act performed on them.
topics.reason: The word is nominative with a 3mp possessive suffix and serves as subject of the nominal clause.

topics.headline: nominative clause stability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the nominative reading gives clothing an independent stable predication, while the accusative variant would pull it back toward adornment syntax.
topics.reason: Canonical nominative makes the word subject of a verbless clause; the CRITICAL variant evidence preserves the alternate accusative pressure.

topics.headline: covering root narrowed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels reward as a whole-body covering of honor, while armor and confusion senses are kept out of the local meaning.
topics.reason: The silk predicate and possessive garment noun select clothing/covering rather than armor or obscuring confusion.

topics.headline: clothing echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees moral clothing and worldly wearing echoes reappear as owned silk identity in the reward scene.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete links to 7:26 and 35:12 and to the pairing of passive adornment with possessed clothing.

words.gloss_range: second fused locative, in it/within it, returning to the gardens in the clothing clause
words.prose: The second {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) brings the clothing predicate back inside the same garden-domain. It prevents the silk clause from floating as a general statement about garments and makes silk a condition of residence there. By repeating the earlier locative before the final material predicate, the ayah completes a two-clause containment frame: the place governs both applied ornaments and possessed clothing.

topics.headline: second garden locative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees silk clothing as located inside the garden residence, not as a general material statement.
topics.reason: The fused preposition-pronoun modifies the clothing predicate and refers back to the gardens.

topics.headline: completed containment frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated locative making one place govern the whole visual economy of ornaments and clothing.
topics.reason: This second locative answers the first and binds the final clause to the same garden antecedent.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative concrete noun, silk, as final material predicate of their clothing
words.root_gloss_range: silk textile, free/noble status, heat/intensity, and refinement branches; the local clothing predicate selects silk while allowing distant status and contrastive heat pressure
words.prose: {{ar:حَرِيرٌ}} ({{tr:ḥarīrun}}) closes the ayah as the predicate of libāsuhum: their clothing is silk. Its indefinite concrete noun form gives material texture rather than a counted garment or loose adjective, and the preceding fīhā keeps that texture inside the garden residence. The {{ar:ح ر ر}} ({{tr:ḥ-r-r}}) root's freedom and heat branches do not replace the silk sense; they remain narrowed pressures of noble release and redirected intensity, especially against the same-surah heat field at 35:21. The final word settles motion and adornment into stable tactile refinement, repeats the exact garment seal of 22:23, links with 76:12 as reward clothing, and frames the ayah from enclosing garden to body-covering silk.

topics.headline: silk material predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader ends on clothing substance and texture rather than on another action or inventory item.
topics.reason: The noun is the predicate of the clothing subject and functions as a concrete material predicate.

topics.headline: root branch refinement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels silk as refined softness with distant noble and intensity echoes, while the garment context blocks heat as the selected meaning.
topics.reason: The clothing subject selects silk, and other root branches can only color the selected textile sense.

topics.headline: formulaic final seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the final silk predicate as a known paradise-garment seal and as the ayah's tactile closure.
topics.reason: Rows cite the exact recurrence with 22:23, the reward-clothing link with 76:12, and the local final-position effect.

topics.headline: cover frame and sound chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah framed from enclosing garden to covering silk, with the tanwīn chain audibly tying permanence, gold, pearl, and silk together.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly connect opening garden enclosure, final silk covering, and the clustered indefinite endings across the reward items.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Word 1 supplies a screened garden, word 3 crosses into it, and words 7 and 11 place concentric forms of enclosure on the body; the locative is repeated.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse contracts protection from habitat to wrist to skin. Entry does not end at arrival: the entrants become bodily fitted to the protected interior they inhabit.

activation_trace.role: A garden screened by its growth supplies the outer inhabited enclosure.
Literal passage into an interior makes the promised place a crossed boundary.
The ornament literally circles the wrist and miniaturizes the garden's enclosure on the body.
Bodily covering completes the nested sequence at skin scale.

changed_reading.before: A destination followed by a list of luxury goods.
changed_reading.after: A sequence of benevolent enclosures in which place, ornament, and clothing progressively secure the entrant.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive adornment at word 4 is followed by metal, pearl, and a garment whose location is again specified.
baseline_models.mechanism: Adornment acts as a visible description of the entrants rather than merely property near them. Metal color, pearl light, and fine cloth make an inwardly changed condition outwardly legible.

activation_trace.role: Literal ornament grounds the passive transformation in something worn.
The branch of description lets ornament function as a visible account of the wearer.
The red-yellow color range supplies chromatic visibility to the bodily display.
Visible shimmer makes the transformed state radiate rather than remain private.
Fine cloth gives the visible state a continuous tactile surface.

changed_reading.after: The entrants are made visibly readable through color, radiance, and clothing; the objects describe a transformed state.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The final garment combines the clothing root with a silk root whose inventory also carries freedom and release from defect.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse can hold protection without hardness: covering and even armor-like security remain, but silk recodes them as free, refined, and non-coercive rather than defensive confinement.

activation_trace.role: Wearable protection supplies the defensive side of clothing.
Freedom from bondage converts covering from restraint into release.
Freedom from flaw gives the textile an ethical and material refinement.
Literal fine silk keeps the release reading anchored in the stated garment.

changed_reading.before: Silk is a luxury textile added after jewelry.
changed_reading.after: Silk is an exploratory material figure for protected freedom: a covering that secures without binding.

context_deltas.mechanism: The early opening-and-withholding contrast converts entry into granted access. The garden remains enclosed, but its boundary is opened as mercy and cannot be barred by a competing holder.

activation_trace.role: Entry into an interior is the focus-side event needing access.
Opening a closure and widening an entrance supplies the access mechanism.
Merciful tenderness identifies the opened access as gift rather than conquest.
Holding or restraining supplies the blocked alternative that the context denies.

structural_cues: 35:2 places opening, mercy, and failed withholding before 35:33's movement into an interior.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an opened mercy that no one can hold back and a later entrance; I treat the former as the causal access condition for the latter. The live alternative is that 35:2 governs providence generally and does not specify this doorway.

changed_reading.before: The entrants simply cross into a bounded garden.
changed_reading.after: They cross a boundary opened as mercy, so enclosure and accessibility become complementary rather than opposed.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier passive beautification makes bad action look good; the focus uses another passive adornment scene. The warning makes final beauty diagnostic only when exterior, wearer, and destination agree, turning it into the counter-image of a deceptive surface.

activation_trace.role: Making beauty appear supplies the earlier case in which an attractive exterior misdescribes action.
Literal bestowed ornament supplies the later visible surface.
Adornment as description lets the later exterior truthfully characterize its wearer.

structural_cues: 35:8 and 35:33 both foreground passive adornment, but the former joins it to mis-seeing bad action while the latter follows garden entry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two passive adornment scenes with opposite settings; I infer a deceptive-versus-vindicated contrast. A live alternative is that the two distinct adornment verbs are not intended as a formal pair.

changed_reading.before: The ornaments are self-evident tokens of honor.
changed_reading.after: Their force lies in being a truthful exterior after the surah has shown that beauty can lie; setting and wearer validate the surface.

context_deltas.mechanism: The worldly scene has people bring ornament out of concealment and put it on themselves while seeking bounty. The focus repeats ornament and clothing but changes the agency: they enter, then are adorned, and their clothing is simply present there. Acquisition becomes reception.

activation_trace.role: Bringing something out of concealment supplies the labor of worldly acquisition.
Literal ornament gives a direct material precursor to the focus adornment.
Active self-covering supplies the worldly agency that the focus recasts.
Gift and beneficence prevent extraction from becoming an autonomous economy.
Passive adornment receives and transforms the earlier ornament action.
The stated garment is possessed in the destination rather than narrated as self-applied.

structural_cues: 35:12 coordinates active extraction and active wearing; 35:33 coordinates active entering with passive adornment and a nominal clothing clause.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated ornament and clothing roots with changed grammar; I infer a shift from human acquisition to bestowed condition. The alternative is that passive voice and nominal possession are ordinary stylistic variation.

changed_reading.before: Paradisal jewelry is a richer version of ornament people obtain and wear in the world.
changed_reading.after: The repeated materials expose a change of agency: worldly ornament is extracted and self-worn, while the final state is received and maintained for its entrants.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same root that names the scorching member of an earlier shade-versus-heat pair returns in the focus as fine silk. The final garment can therefore carry a tactile reversal: destructive heat is not merely absent but revoiced as soft covering and freedom.

activation_trace.role: Protective shade supplies the sheltering pole of the earlier contrast.
Literal heat supplies the hostile tactile state that the focus root later transforms.
Literal silk realizes the same root as a fine wearable surface.
Freedom gives the tactile reversal a release dimension rather than mere climate comfort.

structural_cues: 35:21 opposes shade and scorching heat; 35:33 ends on a silk noun resolved to the same root as that heat.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies root identity and opposite tactile scenes; I supply the arrow from heat to silk as a material reversal. The live alternative is ordinary polysemy with no intended callback.

changed_reading.before: Silk is the last luxury in the list.
changed_reading.after: Silk becomes an embodied reversal of scorching exposure: the threatening root returns as sheltering softness and release.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated differentiation of visible surfaces across fruit, mountains, people, and creatures scales down onto the entrants. Gold color, pearl radiance, and descriptive adornment make created variation wearable rather than merely observed.

activation_trace.role: Visible complexion across fruit and mountains supplies a world-scale field of differentiated surfaces.
Acquiring a new color brings the differentiation from landscape onto living bodies.
The metal's color range condenses the earlier chromatic field into ornament.
Shimmer adds changing light to the entrants' visible surface.
Adornment as description makes the created display characterize its wearer.

structural_cues: 35:27-28 repeat visible differentiation across landscape and bodies immediately before the reward sequence of 35:29-33.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated color taxonomy and later chromatic and luminous materials; I infer a scale change from creation viewed to creation worn. The alternative is a general beauty sequence without this condensation.

changed_reading.before: Gold and pearl indicate undifferentiated wealth.
changed_reading.after: The materials gather the surah's differentiated creation onto human surfaces, making transformed identity visibly particular.

context_deltas.mechanism: A trade that does not perish is first paid in full and then increased. Repeated bounty language surrounds the focus, while one bounty branch itself pictures draped cloth. Jewelry and silk therefore render not the settled wage alone but a gifted surplus that wraps the recipients.

activation_trace.role: Trade and sought profit establish the account-like frame.
Completion without deficiency closes the wage side of the account.
Growth beyond completion opens a surplus after full payment.
Excess and remainder identify the increase as more than equivalence.
Gift and beneficence frame the inherited outcome before the focus.
The rare draped-cloth branch gives surrounding bounty a literal garment-shaped resonance.
The actual garment supplies the focus anchor for surplus becoming wearable.

structural_cues: 35:29-30 moves from non-perishing trade to full payment and then increase; bounty recurs in 35:32 and 35:35 on both sides of 35:33.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies account completion, added bounty, repeated bounty references, and a cloth branch; I infer that the focus materials visualize surplus. The alternative is that every item belongs to recompense generally, with no allocation between wage and increase.

changed_reading.before: The listed goods are the payment owed for prior action.
changed_reading.after: They are the visible and wearable excess that begins only after the account has already been paid in full.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding verse first names selected book-inheritors, then distributes them across three singular class labels. The plural entry can recollect that divided population, making one garden interior hold morally unequal trajectories without erasing their difference.

activation_trace.role: Transmission of book or virtue supplies the broad antecedent group.
Selection defines the group before its internal division.
The middle position makes one distinct trajectory in the three-part distribution.
Precedence supplies the leading trajectory without dissolving the earlier collective.
Permission makes even precedence authorized rather than self-secured.
Plural entry supplies the possible re-gathering of the divided antecedent.

structural_cues: 35:32 begins with one selected inheritor group, partitions it into three generic singular classes, and 35:33 opens with a plural destination clause.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a collective antecedent, internal partition, and following plural; I let the plural resume the broad collective. The materially live alternative is attachment to the nearest leading class alone.

changed_reading.before: The plural entrants are an unspecified rewarded group.
changed_reading.after: One plausible scope gathers all three classes of selected inheritors into the same protected destination despite their unequal paths.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearest class is the one that precedes in good acts by permission, immediately followed by the declaration of great bounty. On this narrower attachment, entry and adornment mark the leading class's distinctive outcome rather than common convergence.

activation_trace.role: Advancing ahead supplies the nearest candidate class for the following plural.
Movement toward beneficial good specifies what distinguishes that class.
Authorization keeps the class's precedence dependent rather than autonomous.
Degree and excellence support a differentiated rather than leveled outcome.
The plural entry is the disputed predicate attached to the nearest class in this model.
Visible description lets adornment mark the class's distinct standing.

structural_cues: The leading-in-good class, its permission phrase, and the great-bounty clause are the nearest material before the plural entry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies proximity and a differentiated leading class; I allow nearest-class attachment. The equally live alternative is that the plural reaches back over all three classes to the original selected collective.

changed_reading.before: The plural entrants are an unspecified rewarded group.
changed_reading.after: A second plausible scope restricts the regalia-bearing entrants to the foremost class, preserving rank differentiation at the threshold.

context_deltas.mechanism: The gold root repeatedly carries going or removal, becomes metal in the focus, and immediately returns as caused removal of sorrow. At the hinge, what departs changes: neither the self nor the rewarded people are sent away; grief is, while gold remains on the body.

activation_trace.role: Going supplies the earlier danger of a self being spent in regret.
Caused removal supplies the possibility that people themselves are made to pass away.
Literal gold arrests the repeated root as a durable object on the entrant.
Immediate caused removal redirects the root's motion onto sorrow.
The roughness of grief identifies what is removed from the newly adorned body.

structural_cues: The focus's metal use of the root is followed in the next ayah by the same root as removal of sorrow, after earlier going and removal uses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies recurrence and immediate juxtaposition; I infer a semantic pivot in what is allowed to go. The live alternative is unactivated homonymy between metal and motion.

changed_reading.before: Gold is a static precious material.
changed_reading.after: Gold becomes a durable marker of selective departure: grief has gone, while the entrants and their adornment remain.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah turns arrival into settled residence and negates both exertion and fatigue. The repeated locative around jewelry and clothing therefore marks an ongoing habitat fitted to the body, not a brief investiture ceremony.

activation_trace.role: The screened garden supplies the habitat whose duration is clarified next.
Entry supplies the initial transition that becomes settlement.
Taking up a place converts arrival into lodging.
Residence and belonging to a home give the garden social and spatial continuity.
Staying in a place supplies explicit duration to the residence.
Exhausting toil is named as a condition that no longer reaches the residents.
Weakness and fatigue are excluded from the continuing bodily state.
Continuous covering ties bodily ease to the permanent environment.

structural_cues: 35:35 immediately resumes the speakers of 35:34, names their permanent abode, and twice negates bodily strain within it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate continuation from entry to residence and no fatigue; I read 35:35 as a temporal gloss on 35:33's repeated locative. The alternative is that permanence describes only the abode and adds nothing to the ornaments.

changed_reading.before: Entry culminates in a moment of ceremonial adornment.
changed_reading.after: Entry opens into permanent, effortless habitation; jewelry and silk are stable properties of life there, not temporary regalia.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the wrist-ornament branch belongs to holding verbs in 35:2 and 35:41, not to an ornament token there. It remains anchored because that exact branch meets the focus bracelet and the context contrasts withheld mercy with cosmic preservation. Render it only as an exploratory topology of benevolent holding, never as a lexical gloss of either verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus bracelet encircles the wrist inside an enduring protected place.

activation_trace.role: The root's wrist-ornament branch places a bracelet image inside the denied act of withholding mercy.
Literal holding supplies preservation of the larger created order.
Departure from place or state names the collapse that holding prevents.
The literal wrist-circling ornament anchors the small-scale bodily version of holding.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it figures a sustaining hold that neither withholds mercy nor permits the adorned life to lapse.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The reading crosses distant branches of the garden root, so it must not claim that the focus garden means a grave. It remains valid as a transformation of shared concealment: resurrection and graves activate a move from burial-covering to living, protective enclosure. Downstream prose should mark it as a spatial resonance, not an alternate dictionary sense in context.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Word 1 names the garden through a root whose inventory includes both vegetated screening and burial concealment.

activation_trace.role: Reviving the dead supplies the transfer out of death rather than mere relocation.
Burial concealment supplies the prior enclosure from which the transformed reading departs.
The root's burial-covering branch keeps the former enclosure attached to the focus word without replacing its surface sense.
The living screened garden supplies the new enclosure after emergence.

changed_reading.before: The garden is only the destination reached after resurrection.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, resurrection changes the mode of concealment itself: burial covering is reopened as a living and protective garden enclosure.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The garment branch of bounty is rare and cross-domain, so it should not replace the ordinary gift or surplus sense. It remains unusually well anchored because bounty recurs immediately before and after a focus verse that explicitly supplies clothing. Render it as a secondary materialization: generosity wraps the recipients.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus ends by assigning the entrants a garment within the garden.

activation_trace.role: The draped-cloth side branch gives the first nearby bounty occurrence a wearable shape.
The bounty occurrence directly before the focus repeats the wrapping image.
The bounty occurrence directly after the focus completes the verbal frame around the garment.
Literal bodily covering anchors the repeated side-branch image in an explicit focus object.

changed_reading.before: Bounty causes or funds the clothing reward.
changed_reading.after: At the exploratory material level, bounty itself wraps the entrants and becomes their garment.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This depends on the packet's non-dominant mapped root for the lodging verb and is therefore form-distant. It remains structurally legitimate because the split inventory explicitly supplies the same adornment root used in the focus, beside ordinary lodging and clothing branches. Render it as an audible or latent convergence of installation and investiture, never as a claim that the lodging verb literally means adornment here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus pairs entry, passive adornment, and clothing; the next ayah names being installed in the permanent residence.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary taking up of a place grounds the next ayah in actual residence.
The same dominant inventory also carries a suit of clothes, linking installation to investiture.
The non-dominant mapped target supplies ornament as a latent side activation of the lodging event.
The explicit focus adornment anchors the side activation to the actual verse.
The explicit focus garment anchors the clothing side of the convergence.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, being installed in the permanent home and being invested with its clothing are two surfaces of one transformation.

strongest_changes: The repeated ornament and clothing roots change agency from extraction and self-wearing in 35:12 to bestowed and continuously possessed adornment in 35:33.
The metal root becomes a semantic hinge: earlier people or the self may go, but after the focus gold remains while sorrow is made to depart.
The heat root returns as silk, allowing the final garment to embody a tactile reversal from scorching exposure to soft protection and freedom.
Full payment followed by increase, plus repeated bounty on both sides of the focus, makes the jewelry and garment readable as gifted surplus rather than equivalent wages.
The plural entry retains two plausible scopes: all three selected inheritor classes may converge, or the nearest foremost class may be singled out.
summary.what_was_special: Direct root recurrences across the focus changed material nouns into transitions of agency, climate, and affect. Rare packet branches also made holding resemble a bracelet, bounty resemble draped cloth, and the next ayah's split lodging root resonate with adornment without displacing ordinary senses.
remaining_uncertainties: The antecedent range of the plural entry remains genuinely forked between the broad selected group and the nearest foremost class.
The metal/removal and heat/silk pivots may be deliberate semantic reversals or simply activated polysemy.
The passive adornment does not state its agent inside the focus ayah, so the bestowal reading depends on grammatical contrast and surrounding gift language.
The wrist-hold, garment-bounty, and split-root lodging activations are valid exploratory resonances but should not be promoted to direct lexical glosses.

baseline.text: Kalıcı cennetlere girerler. Orada altın bilezikler ve incilerle süslenirler; oradaki giysileri ipektir.

findings.text: Bahçeye giriş, sakinleri kat kat içeri alan, örten ve çevreyle bütünleştiren koruyucu bir bolluğa katılmaktır.
Bilezik, inci ve ipek, yalnız sergilenen değerler değil, bedeni çevreleyip güvenli aidiyeti görünür kılan koruyucu katmanlardır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Arrival becomes secure habitation when entry, residence, bodily adornment, and relief from exhausting contact all stabilize together.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The scene is architectural and somatic at once: a granted residence is fitted to the body with wrist ornaments and garments, while pain, grief, and fatigue lose the capacity to make contact.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Entry and lasting residence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Entrants cross a threshold, are settled in a house-like station, and remain there as residents rather than temporary visitors.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: permanent residence (quranic:root_000992:B001/m01); settling in a place (quranic:root_000351:B002/m01); dwelling or fixed abode (quranic:root_001273:B006/m01); resident attached to a house (quranic:root_000499:B007/m01); entering an enclosure (quranic:root_000464:B001/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 35:33 `يَدْخُلُ` (د خ ل); 35:35 `أَحَلَّ/دَارَ/مُقَامَةِ` (ح ل ل/د و ر/ق و م). The surface root ع د ن is unavailable in the bundle, so its permanent-residence motif cannot receive a token-level anchor.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Entry is only the threshold operation. Settlement, house attachment, and permanent residence convert passage into a stable condition whose defining feature is not merely location but non-expulsion.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Arrival becomes secure habitation when entry, residence, bodily adornment, and relief from exhausting contact all stabilize together.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The scene is architectural and somatic at once: a granted residence is fitted to the body with wrist ornaments and garments, while pain, grief, and fatigue lose the capacity to make contact.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Ornament fitted to the body
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Precious material is fashioned into wrist ornaments and paired with lustrous stones and clothing that complete the inhabitant's visible presentation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: bodily ornament (quranic:root_000353:B001/m01); bracelet worn at the wrist (quranic:root_000758:B004/m01); wrist ornament (quranic:root_001424:B006/m01); gold as precious material (quranic:root_000522:B001/m01); pearl as ornament (quranic:root_001337:B001/m01); pearl-like lustre (quranic:root_001337:B002/m01); garment worn on the body (quranic:root_001341:B001/m01); silk fabric (quranic:root_000306:B010/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 35:33 `يُحَلَّ/أَسَاوِرَ/ذَهَبٍ/لُؤْلُؤًا/لِبَاسُ/حَرِيرٌ` (ح ل ي/س و ر/ذ ه ب/ل ء ل ء/ل ب س/ح ر ر); 35:41 `يُمْسِكُ/أَمْسَكَ` (م س ك).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Adornment is assembled as a material sequence: substance, formed ornament, bodily placement, lustre, and garment. This keeps the scene from collapsing into a generic sign of wealth.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: What is hidden within or beyond ordinary perception remains fully knowable and can be brought into evidentiary view.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The channel distinguishes concealment, inward source, visual reception, insight, and public manifestation instead of treating knowledge and sight as interchangeable.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Concealed source and inward content
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A content is withheld from ordinary eyes, lodged in the chest or heart as a source of action, yet remains available to complete knowledge.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: concealment from sight (quranic:root_001117:B001/m01); chest as inner enclosure (quranic:root_000849:B001/m01); chest as source of outward acts (quranic:root_000849:B004/m01); hidden heart or inward core (quranic:root_000266:B010/m01); knowledge of inner conditions (quranic:root_000387:B001/m01); comprehensive knowledge (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Hiddenness is a limit on ordinary reception, not on knowability. Chest, heart, and inner condition locate the source from which action issues, making later judgment responsive to concealed formation as well as visible deed.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P3 (35:31-45) Historical Tracks and Governed Change
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Human succession moves along inherited tracks toward an appointed outcome, while the governing pattern itself resists substitution or diversion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Road wear, doctrinal path, alternation, postponement, and arrival turn history into movement whose local occupants change but whose governing route and endpoint remain stable.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Traveled way and inherited custom
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Repeated movement wears a recognizable road; later travelers follow it as both physical route and inherited practice.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: customary governing path (quranic:root_000750:B001/m01); journeying through land (quranic:root_000769:B001/m01); way or established custom (quranic:root_000769:B002/m01); path or adopted doctrine (quranic:root_000522:B007/m01); straight directed path (quranic:root_001230:B002/m01); road worn by passage (quranic:root_001046:B011/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The invariant pattern is not only a rule but a traveled way made legible by repetition. Physical journey, moral direction, and inherited custom remain distinguishable while explaining why earlier outcomes can instruct later occupants.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalı örtme, duyulardan gizleme ve bir örtünün arkasına saklanma çekirdeğinde kurar; içte saklama ile insanı örten giysi de bu çekirdeğin açık gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca örtme ve gizlenme alanındadır; akıl yitimi, bahçe ve görünmeyen varlık anlamlarını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalı kapsar ve başka dallara ya da yalnızca belirli bir söz öbeğine bağlı anlamları içeri almaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi duyuların erişiminden çıkaracak biçimde örtmek ya da gizlemek; kişinin bir şeyin arkasına saklanması, bir şeyi içinde saklaması ve insanı örten giysi bu çekirdeğin gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir şey örtülerek ya da gizlenerek duyuların erişiminden çıkarılır.
Bir örtünün arkasına saklanma, bir şeyi içinde saklama ve insanı örten giysi aynı gizleme çekirdeğine dayanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak ekseni, bir şeyi duyusal algıdan örterek gizlemek ve bu örtünün sağladığı saklılık durumudur.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir nesnenin örtülmesini, bir kişinin saklanmasını veya örtü işlevli bir şeyi birlikte temsil eden en geniş karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Örtme işlemini, duyulardan gizlenme sonucunu ve dalın genel kapsamını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir öznenin nesneyi görünmez veya algılanamaz duruma getirdiği geçişli kullanımlarda doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Geçişli örtme eylemini ve bunun doğurduğu gizlenme sonucunu eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin bir örtü veya engel aracılığıyla kendini duyulardan sakladığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Örtü aracını ve öznenin kendisini algıdan saklaması anlamını birlikte korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: örtmek; gizleyecek bir örtü sağlamak; içinde saklamak
